title: An inverse limit of flat modules over the quotients A/I^n is flat over a Noetherian A
statement: Let $A$ be a Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] and $I\subseteq A$ an ideal. Let $(M_n)_{n\ge1}$ be an inverse system of $A$-modules, with $A$-linear transition maps $M_{n+1}\to M_n$, such that (1) for every $n$, $I^nM_n=0$ and $M_n$ is a flat $A/I^n$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], and (2) every transition map $M_{n+1}\to M_n$ is surjective. Let $M=\varprojlim_nM_n$ (compatible sequences $(x_n)_n$, $x_n\in M_n$, with componentwise $A$-module structure). Then $M$ is a flat $A$-module, and for every finitely generated $A$-module $Q$ the canonical map $Q\otimes_AM\to\varprojlim_nQ\otimes_AM_n$ is an isomorphism.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 0912 (lemma-limit-flat, line 6475); its proof uses Lemma Tag 0911 (lemma-tor-strictly-pro-zero, line 6449), Homology Lemma Tag 070E (homology-lemma-apply-Mittag-Leffler-again) and Algebra Lemma Tag 00HD (lemma-flat)

proof.text: Conventions. For $m\ge n$ write $p_{mn}:M_m\to M_n$ for the composite transition map and $p_n:M\to M_n$ for the projections. Let $Q$ be a finitely generated $A$-module [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-free-resolution-noetherian] ($A$ is Noetherian) choose an exact complex $\cdots\to F_2\xrightarrow{d_2}F_1\xrightarrow{d_1}F_0\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}Q\to0$ with $F_i\cong A^{\oplus t_i}$ finite free. For every $A$-module $N$ the complex $F_\bullet\otimes_AN$ computes Tor: $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,N)=\ker(d_1\otimes1)/\operatorname{im}(d_2\otimes1)$, functorially in $N$ [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]; and by right exactness of $-\otimes_AN$ applied to $F_1\to F_0\to Q\to0$ [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact], $\varepsilon\otimes1$ induces an isomorphism $\operatorname{coker}(d_1\otimes1_N)\cong Q\otimes_AN$, natural in $N$. So $F_2\otimes_AN\to F_1\otimes_AN\to F_0\otimes_AN$ is a complex with homology $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,N)$ in degree 1 and $Q\otimes_AN$ in degree 0, naturally in $N$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0912, lines 6489--6497 (finite free resolution: Algebra, Lemma 00LP; Tor as in Algebra, Section 00LY)

proof.text: Tor of the levels. Fix $n\ge1$ and write $A_n=A/I^n$. Since $I^nM_n=0$, $M_n$ is an $A_n$-module and $M_n/I^nM_n=M_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-over-quotient-ring] (2) (with $J=I^n$, the $A_n$-module $M_n$ in the role of its $A$ and $F$ in the role of its $M$) and (1), there are isomorphisms $M_n\otimes_AF\cong M_n\otimes_{A_n}(F/I^nF)\cong M_n\otimes_{A_n}(A_n\otimes_AF)$, natural in the $A$-module $F$ and in the $A_n$-module $M_n$; hence (after the symmetry of $\otimes$) an isomorphism of complexes $F_\bullet\otimes_AM_n\cong(F_\bullet\otimes_AA_n)\otimes_{A_n}M_n$, $f\otimes x\mapsto(f\otimes1)\otimes x$. As $M_n$ is a flat $A_n$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map], the functor $-\otimes_{A_n}M_n$ on $A_n$-modules preserves injections and (by [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact]) cokernels, so it is exact, and by [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] it commutes with homology. Therefore $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,M_n)\cong\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,A/I^n)\otimes_{A/I^n}M_n$, $[\sum f_k\otimes x_k]\mapsto\sum[f_k\otimes1]\otimes x_k$ on cycles of the form $\sum_k(f_k\otimes1)\otimes x_k$. For $m\ge n$ these isomorphisms are compatible with the transition maps: the map $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,M_m)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,M_n)$ induced by $p_{mn}$ corresponds to $\tau_{mn}\otimes p_{mn}:[z]\otimes x\mapsto\tau_{mn}([z])\otimes p_{mn}(x)$, where $\tau_{mn}:\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,A/I^m)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,A/I^n)$ is induced by $A/I^m\to A/I^n$ (check on the elements $(f\otimes\bar a)\otimes x$, which generate $(F_1\otimes_AA_m)\otimes_{A_m}M_m$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0912, lines 6497--6505 ('Tor_1(Q, M_n) = Tor_1(Q, A/I^n) (x)_{A/I^n} M_n as M_n is flat over A/I^n')

proof.text: The Tor systems are essentially zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-strictly-pro-zero] (with $p=1$ and the finite module $Q$) there is $c>0$ such that $\tau_{n,n-c}=0$ for all $n\ge c$. By Step 2, for $n\ge1$ the transition map $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,M_{n+c})\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,M_n)$ is $\tau_{n+c,n}\otimes p_{n+c,n}=0$. Consequently the inverse system $T_n=\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,M_n)$ (i) is ML: $\operatorname{Im}(T_k\to T_n)=0$ for all $k\ge n+c$ (take $c(n)=n+c$ in the definition of [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-complex-limit-homology]); (ii) is essentially constant in the sense of that node, with $X=0$, $i_0=1$: $X\to T_1\to X$ is $\mathrm{id}_0$ and for every $j$ the map $T_{j+c}\to T_j$ is $0$, the composite through $X=0$; (iii) has $\varprojlim_nT_n=0$: a compatible sequence $(z_n)$ has $z_n=$ image of $z_{n+c}$, which is $0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0912, lines 6505--6506 ('By Lemma 0911 we see that this system is essentially constant (with value 0)')

proof.text: $Q\otimes_AM\cong\varprojlim_nQ\otimes_AM_n$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-complex-limit-homology] to the inverse system of complexes $A^{-2}_n=F_2\otimes_AM_n\to A^{-1}_n=F_1\otimes_AM_n\to A^0_n=F_0\otimes_AM_n\to A^1_n=0$ with transition maps $1\otimes p_{n+1,n}$. Its hypotheses hold: under $F_i\cong A^{\oplus t_i}$ the map $F_i\otimes_AM_{n+1}\to F_i\otimes_AM_n$ is $p_{n+1,n}^{\oplus t_i}$, surjective, so $(A^{-2}_n)$ and $(A^{-1}_n)$ are ML with $c(n)=n$ (images of surjective maps are everything; Stacks, Algebra Example 0596); $H^{-1}_n=\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q,M_n)$ (Step 1) is essentially constant (Step 3). Its conclusion: $H^0$ of the limit complex maps isomorphically onto $\varprojlim_nH^0_n=\varprojlim_nQ\otimes_AM_n$ (Step 1). The limit complex is $F_2\otimes_AM\to F_1\otimes_AM\to F_0\otimes_AM$: the canonical maps $F_i\otimes_AM\to\varprojlim_nF_i\otimes_AM_n$, $f\otimes x\mapsto(f\otimes p_n(x))_n$, are isomorphisms since under $F_i\cong A^{\oplus t_i}$ they become $M^{\oplus t_i}\to\varprojlim_n M_n^{\oplus t_i}=(\varprojlim_n M_n)^{\oplus t_i}$, the identity, and they commute with $d_i\otimes1$ (naturality in $F$). So $H^0=\operatorname{coker}(d_1\otimes1_M)\cong Q\otimes_AM$ (Step 1 with $N=M$), and tracing an element $f\otimes x$ shows that the resulting isomorphism $Q\otimes_AM\to\varprojlim_nQ\otimes_AM_n$ is the canonical map $\gamma_Q:q\otimes x\mapsto(q\otimes p_n(x))_n$. This proves the second assertion; $\gamma_Q$ is natural in $Q$ (evident on generators $q\otimes x$).

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0912, lines 6506--6511 (Homology, Lemma 070E; Algebra, Example 0596 for ML of surjective systems)

proof.text: Reduction of flatness. By [lem-weil-pbc-flat-fg-ideal-criterion] it suffices to show that $\mathfrak a\otimes_AM\to A\otimes_AM=M$ is injective for every finitely generated ideal $\mathfrak a\subseteq A$; this is the case $Q=\mathfrak a$, $Q'=A$ of the following claim: for every injective $A$-linear map $u:Q\to Q'$ of finitely generated $A$-modules, $u\otimes1_M:Q\otimes_AM\to Q'\otimes_AM$ is injective. By Step 4 and the naturality of $\gamma$, $\varprojlim_n(u\otimes1_{M_n})\circ\gamma_Q=\gamma_{Q'}\circ(u\otimes1_M)$ with $\gamma_Q,\gamma_{Q'}$ isomorphisms, so $\ker(u\otimes1_M)\cong\ker\big(\varprojlim_nQ\otimes_AM_n\to\varprojlim_nQ'\otimes_AM_n\big)$ and it suffices that the latter kernel is $0$.

source.place: More on Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 0912, lines 6513--6519 (Algebra, Lemma 00HD)

proof.text: The limit of $Q\otimes M_n\to Q'\otimes M_n$ is injective. Let $Q''=\operatorname{coker}u$, a finitely generated $A$-module, so $0\to Q\xrightarrow{u}Q'\xrightarrow{v}Q''\to0$ is exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-tor-long-exact-first-variable], for each $n$ the sequence $\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q',M_n)\to\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q'',M_n)\xrightarrow{\delta}Q\otimes_AM_n\xrightarrow{u\otimes1}Q'\otimes_AM_n$ is exact, and by the naturality in $M_n$ its maps commute with the maps induced by $p_{n+1,n}$: it is an inverse system of complexes $A^{-2}_n\to A^{-1}_n\to A^0_n\to A^1_n$. By Step 3 applied to the finitely generated modules $Q'$ and $Q''$, the systems $(A^{-2}_n)=(\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q',M_n))$ and $(A^{-1}_n)=(\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q'',M_n))$ are ML and $\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q'',M_n)=0$; and $H^{-1}_n=0$ by exactness, an essentially constant system (value $X=0$). By [lem-weil-pbc-mittag-leffler-complex-limit-homology], $H^0$ of the limit complex is $\varprojlim_nH^0_n=0$ (exactness at $A^0_n$), i.e. $\ker\big(\varprojlim_nQ\otimes_AM_n\to\varprojlim_nQ'\otimes_AM_n\big)$ equals the image of $\varprojlim_n\operatorname{Tor}^A_1(Q'',M_n)=0$. So this kernel is $0$; by Step 5, $u\otimes1_M$ is injective, and $M$ is a flat $A$-module [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map].
